summary: Completed backend regression and focused desktop/mobile coverage, hero, navigation, modal, contact, and responsive UI testing. Core flows passed, but the configured hero MP4 is rejected by its external host.

integration_issues.issue: The configured Pexels MP4 returns HTTP 403 twice in the live browser. The video element exists with muted/autoplay/loop/poster attributes, but readyState remains 0 and networkState is 3, so the film layer does not play; the poster fallback is visible.

action_items: Replace the inaccessible Pexels hero MP4 with a permitted/reliable hosted engineering video or a bundled asset, then verify autoplay and no console 403 errors. Preserve the existing poster fallback.
critical_code_review_comments: Hero video source is hardcoded to an external Pexels URL that currently denies browser requests with 403; this violates the no broken new asset-load requirement and leaves the intended film layer inactive.
seed_data_creation: Created TEST-prefixed contact inquiries and status records through the public regression suite; no seeded production data was modified.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend root/contact validation/status persistence passed. Desktop coverage globe and all four sector status updates, capability tabs, case-study scroll stages, relationship panel, contact success, mobile navigation, and 390px overflow passed. All page images and poster loaded; only the external hero MP4 returned 403 and emitted console errors.
rca of the issue: App.js dynamically creates video.hero-film with src=https://videos.pexels.com/video-files/853800/853800-hd_1920_1080_30fps.mp4. Live response inspection recorded HTTP 403 for that URL, leaving the media element in networkState 3 with MediaError code 4. The poster URL remains valid, which masks the missing motion layer visually but does not satisfy the autoplay-film requirement.
test_credentials: Not applicable; no authentication flow was requested.
